A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe RLHF-V work despite changes to the title and format. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment win rates, guard-model classification and moderation results, preference-data and multiplier ablations, and qualitative alignment cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark, baseline, and guard-model comparisons in Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: v2 introduces an explicit projected multiplier update in Equation 8. However, v1 already describes an upper bound on the multiplier, and both versions retain the same logarithmic update in Appendix A.3. The PDFs leave unresolved whether the implemented optimization procedure changed or received a different, unreconciled description; the reward/cost models and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Table 3 extends image-text safety and helpfulness evaluation from three benchmark datasets to five by adding VLGuard and VLSBench. Table 2b also extends guard-classification evaluation to SPA-VL and separate MM-SafetyBench input categories. This substantially broadens evaluation coverage while retaining the original training data and modality.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds MM-RLHF trained with helpfulness preferences and safety preferences across all three backbone models, including comparisons on the original benchmarks. The existing RLHF-V, LLaVA-RLHF, DPO, PPO, and Llama-Guard comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 1 replace the blank-image control with text-only input, changing the reported image-contribution protocol. The guard evaluation distinguishes binary and multilevel variants and adds benchmark-specific accuracy/F1 reporting. The main alignment evaluation retains GPT-4o judging, win-rate metrics, and the Appendix C prompts.

E4.justification: v2 Table 2a adds a direct binary-versus-multilevel Beaver-Guard-V comparison addressing label granularity. The image-contribution analysis uses a revised control. The preference-data-size ablation, multiplier sensitivity analysis, training curves, and three Appendix D case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added plus/minus annotations in v2 Table 3 are differences from the 0.5 reference score, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive VLGuard/VLSBench, MM-RLHF, and guard-classification results. Table 1 reports replacement ASRs under revised input controls. v1's single guard accuracy of 0.86 becomes separate binary and multilevel entries of 0.78 and 0.85, with changed variant descriptions. All 144 comparable values from the original main alignment table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds Equation 8 and defines projection of the multiplier onto [0, νmax], introducing an explicit mathematical update involving budget term b. The CMDP formulation, existing losses, and Appendix A equations are retained. No new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: v2 adds a contribution claim that the budget bound addresses unstable multimodal optimization and emphasizes the difficulty of directly transferring Safe RLHF. The central dataset, guardrail, and constrained-alignment contributions remain, as do the headline 34.2% safety and 34.3% helpfulness improvements.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking annotation disagreement to different visual focuses and training instability to multimodal optimization, attributing stabilization to the budget bound. Table 3 explicitly prioritizes safety when interpreting the trade-off. The conclusion also explicitly identifies generalization beyond image-text settings as a limitation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the multiplier projection interval in Section 4.3. Conversely, v1's prose describing invalid-prompt filtering and final manual prompt review is omitted, although the pipeline graphic remains. Appendix A's PPO, KL, and PTX implementation information and the repository access statement are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on language-model safety failures and safeguards, including SafeInfer and LISA, alongside OmniSafe and MM-RLHF. It newly positions direct transfer of language-only Safe RLHF as insufficient. The existing discussion of multimodal alignment methods and safety datasets remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around explicit multimodal challenges, the conclusion is rewritten, and data-construction prose is condensed and partly relocated to Appendix B. The title and author list change, and the author-contribution paragraph is removed. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main paper switches from two columns to one. v2 substantially expands and reformats the comparison tables, replaces the moderation illustration with a composite figure incorporating the existing moderation-round results, merges the multiplier plots, and moves the harmful-category example figure into the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added VLGuard/VLSBench evaluations and MM-RLHF comparisons test the central safety-helpfulness claim against additional data and a relevant multimodal competitor. The binary-versus-multilevel guard comparison also strengthens evidence for the annotation design. These provide a modest net improvement, tempered by the unresolved relationship between v2's projected update in Equation 8 and the retained logarithmic update in Appendix A.3.
